title: Move each @grafting/ui component's Props interface + TSDoc (incl. @layer/@status/@example) into its own implementation file; index.ts becomes a pure re-export barrel
objective: Owner-directed follow-up to UI-DOC-MESH-TSDOC-EXAMPLES: 'eu faço esses comentarios quando eu crio o componente para toda função que tem export, dentro do index eu apenas faço o export global. funcionaria?' -- owner chose the 'só a reorganização de arquivos agora' option after being shown that this requires fixing tools/scripts/check-typescript-public-api.mjs (Storybook Controls/argTypes generation deferred to a later task). Today every Props interface, its per-field TSDoc, the public wrapper function, and its @layer/@status/@example tags all live directly in packages/ui/src/index.ts; the real JSX implementation lives in a separate atoms/molecules/*.tsx 'View' file. This task collapses that split: each component's own file (e.g. atoms/text.tsx) becomes the single source of truth (Props interface with field docs + the public function with its full TSDoc, renamed from e.g. TextView to Text), and index.ts becomes nothing but named re-exports. Two consumers currently assume every exported declaration lives directly in index.ts and must be taught to resolve through a local re-export to the original declaration: check-typescript-public-api.mjs (both its 'every export must have TSDoc/every interface member must have TSDoc' check, and its baseline renderer, which must inline the re-exported file's own full declaration text instead of showing a bare passthrough re-export line -- verified via a scratch spike that plain tsc emits only a thin `export { X } from './y.js'` passthrough into index.d.ts, not an expanded signature) and packages/ui/scripts/export-doc-mesh.mjs (must build a real ts.Program + type checker instead of a standalone parsed source file, so it can resolve each re-exported name to its real declaration in whichever file it lives, the same way TypeDoc already does natively for docs/generated/api/ts/ui.api.md -- confirmed generate-api-docs.mjs needs no change since it already uses real TypeDoc, which follows re-exports out of the box). Also relocates atoms/data-table.tsx to organisms/data-table.tsx while touching it, correcting a pre-existing layer/path mismatch already flagged in UI-DOC-MESH-TSDOC-EXAMPLES's risks (its layer was always documented/treated as organism despite living under atoms/). A few genuinely cross-component vocabulary types (UiStatus, CardShape, UiMountHandle<Props>) move to a new packages/ui/src/shared-types.ts rather than being owned by one component's file.
validations: TODO: spike (already run in a scratch dir, not tracked) confirmed plain tsc emits a bare `export { X } from './y.js'` passthrough into index.d.ts for a local re-export -- the full signature only appears in the target file's own emitted .d.ts. check-typescript-public-api.mjs's baseline renderer must inline that target content so the tracked baseline stays one complete, reviewable document instead of regressing to opaque passthrough lines.

risks: This is the more invasive of the two options the owner was offered; check-typescript-public-api.mjs is shared enforcement infrastructure (not packages/ui-specific), so its resolution-through-re-exports behavior must stay correct for the existing direct-declaration case too (every other TypeScript project in the repo still declares everything directly in its entry point) -- verified by keeping that code path unchanged and only adding a new branch for ExportDeclaration-with-moduleSpecifier statements.

antd's own Button export collides with the package's public Button name in atoms/button.tsx -- aliased on import (`import { Button as AntButton } from "antd"`) rather than renamed at the boundary, so the public export stays named Button as today.
